title: Facility Investment Services for Marine Corp Air Station (MCAS) Cherry Point North Carolina and outlying fields Bogue, Atlantic, BT 11 and BT 9
description: This is not a request for either a quote or proposal, or invitation for bid. The intent of this pre-solicitation synopsis is to notify potential offerors of a Performance-Based Facility Support Service Type Contract, with Recurring and Non-Recurring Services at Marine Corp Air Station (MCAS) Cherry Point, North Carolina. The contractor shall provide all labor, management, supervision, tools, material, and equipment required to perform Facility Investment Services for facilities, ground structures, and installed equipment and systems at Marine Corp Air Station (MCAS) Cherry Point North Carolina and outlying fields Bogue, Atlantic, BT 11 and BT 9. BT 11 and BT 9 are islands located in the Pamlico Sound, which is accessible only by boat. General Work Requirements: The contractor shall provide facility support services that include, but are not limited to: Service Orders / Ticket Work HVAC Water Testing and Treatment Services Boilers and Unfired Pressure Vessels Boiler Plant Controls Boiler Water Testing and Treatment Services Fire Protection Systems, Fire Suppression, CO2 Fire Suppression Systems Gaylord/Ansul Hoods and Ducts Systems Vertical Transportation Equipment (VTE) Medical Gas Delivery System AV8B Engine Test Cell Annual Cleaning of Hangar Floors Actuator Valves Paint Stripping Booth Equipment Reverse Osmosis Ultra-Violet System Compressed Air Systems Atlas Copco United Blowers Positive Displacement Maintenance Scale Calibration Turnstile and Gate Maintenance Flow Meter Calibration Tool Calibration, including high voltage tools Inspection of Elevated Potable Water Tanks Cathodic Protection Systems Certification and Calibration of Parshall Flumes Calibration, Certification, and Servicing HACH Probes Analyzers and Sensors Calibration, and Certification Gas Monitoring System IWTP B-4380 VTE Certification Support Grease Traps Sewage Plant Sludge Removal and Land Application Alkaline Stabilizing and Stabilized Liquid Sludge Port-A-John Service Sealed Vault Toilet/Septic Tanks Pond Maintenance Aquatic Weed Fisheries Management Source selection procedures will be used to select the best value offeror using tradeoff analysis in accordance with FAR Part 15 � Contracting by Negotiation. The solicitation and resulting contract award will be a performance-based service acquisition made to the responsible offeror whose proposal, conforming to the request for proposal (RFP), will be advantageous to the Government price and other evaluation factors considered. The offeror�s proposal shall contain a response to each of the evaluation factors and shall be in the form prescribed by the solicitation. The solicitation requires the evaluation of price and the following non-price factors: Factor 1 � Management Approach, Factor 2 � Recent, Relevant Experience of the Firm, Factor 3 � Safety, and Factor 4 � Past Performance. The proposed procurement will be issued as an indefinite delivery/indefinite quantity (IDIQ) type contract with recurring and non-recurring services. The IDIQ contract will include online ordering capability using FedMall for the non-recurring exhibit line item numbers (ELINs). Acceptance of Government Purchase Credit Cards is required along with the purchase of FedMall encrypted software. The North American Classification System (NAICS) is 561210; the size standard is $47M. Offers shall be submitted for the performance of work for a period of one year. However, the initial term of the contract may be for a period of less than one year. The Government has the option to extend the term of the contract services for additional periods of one to twelve months. The contract will be for a base period of one year with four (4) one-year option periods, which, cumulatively, will not exceed (60) months. This contract will include a phase-in period. If the Government does not award a follow-on contract in time, the Government may require the Contractor to continue performance for an additional period up to six months under the Option to Extend Services clause. A sources sought notice N4008526R0042 for this procurement was posted on 5 December 2025 on SAM, and a market survey was conducted that included an assessment of relevant qualifications and capabilities of potentially qualified firms. As a result of the market research analysis, a determination was made to set aside this procurement under the Small Business Program. The NAVFAC MIDLANT small business office, as well as the Small Business Association, concurs with this decision. The proposed procurement will be listed as a competitive 100 percent small business set-aside. The Government will only accept offers from small business concerns. The Request for Proposal (RFP) will be made available in electronic format only (Adobe Acrobat (pdf)) and will be posted on SAM.gov website on or about 12 November 2026. The estimated proposal due date shall be at least 30 days after the RFP is posted. All prospective contractors are required to register on the System for Award Management (SAM) database. Offerors and contractors may obtain information on registration and annual confirmation requirements via the Internet at https://sam.gov/. Notifications of any updates or amendments to the solicitation will be posted on the SAM. Only registered contractors will be notified by e-mail when amendments to the solicitation are issued. IT IS THE SOLE RESPONISBILITY OF THE OFFEROR TO CONTINUALLY VIEW THE WEBSITE FOR CHANGES. This contract will replace a contract (N4008521D0034) for similar services awarded in 2021 for $7,184,504.64 (recurring and non-recurring services to Government Contracting Resources, Inc., 315 Page Rd, Pinehurst, NC 28374. title: Maintenance Dredging of the Isle au Haut Thoroughfare near Isle au Haut, Maine
description: The Isle au Haut Thoroughfare Federal Navigation Project, located between Isle au Haut, Maine and Kimball Island, Maine on the outskirts of Penobscot Bay, about six miles southeast of Stonington and 25 miles east of Rockland. The Federal Navigation Project consists of a -6-foot Mean Lower Low Water (MLLW) deep by 75-foot wide extending 1,200-foot in length through the shoal in the thoroughfare.The proposed work consists of mechanically dredging approximately 3,355 cubic yards (cy) (1,183 cy required, plus 2,172 cy overdepth) of shoaled material consisting of highly compacted coarse sand and gravel, with areas of cobbles and isolated small boulders from the channel. Due to the material type, a mechanical dredge with the ability to dig highly compacted coarse sand and gravel will be required. The proposed action is to dredge to the authorized depth of -6-foot MLLW plus an additional 1-foot of required advance maintenance with an additional allowable 1-foot of overdepth (e.g. -7-foot MLLW required + 1-foot allowable OD). One-time, advanced maintenance is approved for the entirety of the 1200-foot long authorized channel. The dredged material will be placed at the Flake Island Disposal Site (FIDS) which is approximately 1 nautical mile northwest of the FNP. Placement of the dredged material (sand, gravel and cobble) at Flake Island Disposal Site will benefit both juvenile lobster habitat and juvenile cod by increasing the areas habitat complexity.The anticipated allowable dredging window is between September 15 and April 1 to avoid impacts to spawning shellfish, benthic resources, Essential Fish Habitat (EFH) of federally managed species, threatened and endangered species and interactions with mobile fishing gear.

title: Maintenance Dredging of the Isle au Haut Thoroughfare near Isle au Haut, Maine
description: The Isle au Haut Thoroughfare Federal Navigation Project, located between Isle au Haut, Maine and Kimball Island, Maine on the outskirts of Penobscot Bay, about six miles southeast of Stonington and 25 miles east of Rockland. The Federal Navigation Project consists of a -6-foot Mean Lower Low Water (MLLW) deep by 75-foot wide extending 1,200-foot in length through the shoal in the thoroughfare.The proposed work consists of mechanically dredging approximately 3,355 cubic yards (cy) (1,183 cy required, plus 2,172 cy overdepth) of shoaled material consisting of highly compacted coarse sand and gravel, with areas of cobbles and isolated small boulders from the channel. Due to the material type, a mechanical dredge with the ability to dig highly compacted coarse sand and gravel will be required. The proposed action is to dredge to the authorized depth of -6-foot MLLW plus an additional 1-foot of required advance maintenance with an additional allowable 1-foot of overdepth (e.g. -7-foot MLLW required + 1-foot allowable OD). One-time, advanced maintenance is approved for the entirety of the 1200-foot long authorized channel. The dredged material will be placed at the Flake Island Disposal Site (FIDS) which is approximately 1 nautical mile northwest of the FNP. Placement of the dredged material (sand, gravel and cobble) at Flake Island Disposal Site will benefit both juvenile lobster habitat and juvenile cod by increasing the areas habitat complexity.The anticipated allowable dredging window is between September 15 and April 1 to avoid impacts to spawning shellfish, benthic resources, Essential Fish Habitat (EFH) of federally managed species, threatened and endangered species and interactions with mobile fishing gear.

NOTICE FOR FILING AGENCY PROTESTS United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) Ombudsman Program The United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) is committed to fair, transparent, and efficient acquisitions. Interested parties with concerns about this solicitation are encouraged to seek resolution through the following USDA procedures. Tier 1: Contracting Officer Concern Resolution Submission: Interested parties with concerns about either the solicitation or subsequent award should first submit their concern directly to the Contracting Officer, providing sufficient detail to allow the Contracting Officer to understand and assess the issue. Process: The Contracting Officer will review the concern, seek clarification as needed, and engage with the interested party to attempt prompt resolution. Review Timeline: The Contracting Officer will make every effort to provide a response or resolution within 10 business days of receiving the concern. Effect on Award or Performance: Tier 1 engagement is not considered an official notification of filing an agency protest and does not pause solicitation deadlines, delay award decisions, or suspend contract performance. Next Steps: If the matter cannot be resolved at Tier 1, the interested party may file a written agency protest under Tier 2. USDA encourages all parties to seek resolution with the Contracting Officer before filing an agency protest. Tier 2: Agency Protest If concerns cannot be resolved at Tier 1, an interested party may file a written agency protest with either the Contracting Officer or the USDA Independent Review Authority. The decision by the USDA Independent Review Authority is an alternative to a decision by the Contracting Officer. The USDA Independent Review Authority will not consider an appeal of the Contracting Officer�s decision on an agency protest. The protest must state whether the protester elects review by the Contracting Officer, by the USDA Independent Review Authority. If no election is stated, the Contracting Officer will decide the protest. Required Information: Protests shall include the information set forth in FAR 33.104-4 (a)(3). Failure to submit the required information may result in a delay or dismissal of the protest. Submission: Agency protests should be submitted electronically to SPE.inquiry@usda.gov and the Contracting Officer. Timeliness: Protests must be filed within the timeframes specified in FAR 33.104. Effect on Award or Performance: Contract awards or performance will be suspended during the protest period unless justified in writing for urgent and compelling reasons or determined to be in the best interest of the Government. Review Timeline: USDA strives to resolve agency-level protests within 35 business days of receipt. Election of Forum: By filing a protest with USDA, the protesters agree not to file a protest on the same matter with the Government Accountability Office (GAO) or any other external forum while the agency protest is pending. If such a protest is filed externally, the USDA agency protest will be dismissed. Questions: Questions regarding this notice or protest procedures should be directed to the Contracting Officer identified in this solicitation.

title: Maintenance Dredging of the Isle au Haut Thoroughfare near Isle au Haut, Maine
description: The Isle au Haut Thoroughfare Federal Navigation Project, located between Isle au Haut, Maine and Kimball Island, Maine on the outskirts of Penobscot Bay, about six miles southeast of Stonington and 25 miles east of Rockland. The Federal Navigation Project consists of a -6-foot Mean Lower Low Water (MLLW) deep by 75-foot wide extending 1,200-foot in length through the shoal in the thoroughfare.The proposed work consists of mechanically dredging approximately 3,355 cubic yards (cy) (1,183 cy required, plus 2,172 cy overdepth) of shoaled material consisting of highly compacted coarse sand and gravel, with areas of cobbles and isolated small boulders from the channel. Due to the material type, a mechanical dredge with the ability to dig highly compacted coarse sand and gravel will be required. The proposed action is to dredge to the authorized depth of -6-foot MLLW plus an additional 1-foot of required advance maintenance with an additional allowable 1-foot of overdepth (e.g. -7-foot MLLW required + 1-foot allowable OD). One-time, advanced maintenance is approved for the entirety of the 1200-foot long authorized channel. The dredged material will be placed at the Flake Island Disposal Site (FIDS) which is approximately 1 nautical mile northwest of the FNP. Placement of the dredged material (sand, gravel and cobble) at Flake Island Disposal Site will benefit both juvenile lobster habitat and juvenile cod by increasing the areas habitat complexity.The anticipated allowable dredging window is between September 15 and April 1 to avoid impacts to spawning shellfish, benthic resources, Essential Fish Habitat (EFH) of federally managed species, threatened and endangered species and interactions with mobile fishing gear.

title: Notice of Intent to Sole Source � NSA Annapolis, Maryland UESC
description: The Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command (NAVFAC) intends to award a Utility Energy Service Contract (UESC) to Baltimore Gas and Electric Company (BGE) for the design, construction, commissioning, and financing of a comprehensive energy resilience project at Naval Support Activity (NSA) Annapolis, Maryland. The proposed project, estimated at approximately $45 million, will include a Combined Heat and Power (CHP) cogeneration plant integrated with a microgrid to enhance installation energy resilience. Major project elements include: A CHP system supporting an estimated 19 MW peak electrical demand, including three natural gas-fired turbines and associated heat-recovery systems; An integrated microgrid control system capable of island-mode operation during utility grid outages; An absorption chiller at the Lejeune Chilled Water Plant (597U) utilizing recovered waste heat; Relocation and upgrade of the 13C-1 electrical substation; Required natural-gas infrastructure upgrades and electric-grid interconnection activities; An Investment Grade Audit (IGA), design, engineering, construction, testing, commissioning, and construction management; and Operator training and project turnover documentation. Basis for Intended Sole Source The Government intends to use other than full and open competition pursuant to 10 U.S.C. � 3204(a)(1) and FAR 6.302-1, Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements. The proposed action will be implemented as a UESC pursuant to 10 U.S.C. � 2913(d). BGE is the franchised electric and natural-gas utility serving NSA Annapolis and owns and operates the affected utility distribution infrastructure. GSA Areawide Public Utility Contract No. 47PA0724D0003 provides for BGE electric, natural-gas, and energy-management services within its franchised service territory. The contemplated UESC requires integrated responsibility for natural-gas capacity upgrades, electric-system interconnection, grid coordination, and modifications affecting BGE-owned or controlled infrastructure. These functions are integral to the CHP, microgrid, and island-mode requirements. The Government issued a Sources Sought Notice on February 5, 2026, which closed on February 20, 2026. Five firms responded to the notice. Based on the Government�s market research, acquisition planning, and review of the responses received, Baltimore Gas and Electric Company (BGE) was determined to be the only responsible source capable of satisfying the Government�s requirements. BGE was the only respondent possessing the requisite utility-service authority, control of the affected infrastructure, and ability to execute or authorize the necessary utility-system modifications and interconnection activities required to perform the contemplated UESC. Submission of Capability Information This notice is not a request for competitive proposals. However, responsible sources that believe they possess the capability, legal authority, and financing capacity to perform the complete requirement may submit a written capability statement. Capability statements should demonstrate: Legal authorization to provide the required electric and natural-gas utility services to NSA Annapolis; Authority and ability to execute or authorize the required utility-infrastructure modifications; Ability to perform and coordinate required electric-grid interconnection activities, including coordination with PJM Interconnection and applicable stakeholders; Experience with projects of comparable size, scope, and complexity under a UESC or comparable utility-financed arrangement; and Ability to provide the financing necessary to implement the project. Responses shall contain sufficient information for the Government to determine whether the respondent can satisfy the complete requirement and shall be submitted electronically in PDF format to olisha.g.costa.civ@us.navy.mil no later than 1:00 PM Eastern Time on Tuesday, November 10, 2026. The Government will consider timely responses before determining whether to proceed with the contemplated sole-source action. Information received will be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. The Government will not pay for information submitted in response to this notice.

title: Maintenance Dredging of the Isle au Haut Thoroughfare near Isle au Haut, Maine
description: The Isle au Haut Thoroughfare Federal Navigation Project, located between Isle au Haut, Maine and Kimball Island, Maine on the outskirts of Penobscot Bay, about six miles southeast of Stonington and 25 miles east of Rockland. The Federal Navigation Project consists of a -6-foot Mean Lower Low Water (MLLW) deep by 75-foot wide extending 1,200-foot in length through the shoal in the thoroughfare.The proposed work consists of mechanically dredging approximately 3,355 cubic yards (cy) (1,183 cy required, plus 2,172 cy overdepth) of shoaled material consisting of highly compacted coarse sand and gravel, with areas of cobbles and isolated small boulders from the channel. Due to the material type, a mechanical dredge with the ability to dig highly compacted coarse sand and gravel will be required. The proposed action is to dredge to the authorized depth of -6-foot MLLW plus an additional 1-foot of required advance maintenance with an additional allowable 1-foot of overdepth (e.g. -7-foot MLLW required + 1-foot allowable OD). One-time, advanced maintenance is approved for the entirety of the 1200-foot long authorized channel. The dredged material will be placed at the Flake Island Disposal Site (FIDS) which is approximately 1 nautical mile northwest of the FNP. Placement of the dredged material (sand, gravel and cobble) at Flake Island Disposal Site will benefit both juvenile lobster habitat and juvenile cod by increasing the areas habitat complexity.The anticipated allowable dredging window is between September 15 and April 1 to avoid impacts to spawning shellfish, benthic resources, Essential Fish Habitat (EFH) of federally managed species, threatened and endangered species and interactions with mobile fishing gear.

title: Maintenance Dredging of the Isle au Haut Thoroughfare near Isle au Haut, Maine
description: The Isle au Haut Thoroughfare Federal Navigation Project, located between Isle au Haut, Maine and Kimball Island, Maine on the outskirts of Penobscot Bay, about six miles southeast of Stonington and 25 miles east of Rockland. The Federal Navigation Project consists of a -6-foot Mean Lower Low Water (MLLW) deep by 75-foot wide extending 1,200-foot in length through the shoal in the thoroughfare.The proposed work consists of mechanically dredging approximately 3,355 cubic yards (cy) (1,183 cy required, plus 2,172 cy overdepth) of shoaled material consisting of highly compacted coarse sand and gravel, with areas of cobbles and isolated small boulders from the channel. Due to the material type, a mechanical dredge with the ability to dig highly compacted coarse sand and gravel will be required. The proposed action is to dredge to the authorized depth of -6-foot MLLW plus an additional 1-foot of required advance maintenance with an additional allowable 1-foot of overdepth (e.g. -7-foot MLLW required + 1-foot allowable OD). One-time, advanced maintenance is approved for the entirety of the 1200-foot long authorized channel. The dredged material will be placed at the Flake Island Disposal Site (FIDS) which is approximately 1 nautical mile northwest of the FNP. Placement of the dredged material (sand, gravel and cobble) at Flake Island Disposal Site will benefit both juvenile lobster habitat and juvenile cod by increasing the areas habitat complexity.The anticipated allowable dredging window is between September 15 and April 1 to avoid impacts to spawning shellfish, benthic resources, Essential Fish Habitat (EFH) of federally managed species, threatened and endangered species and interactions with mobile fishing gear.

NOTICE FOR FILING AGENCY PROTESTS United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) Ombudsman Program The United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) is committed to fair, transparent, and efficient acquisitions. Interested parties with concerns about this solicitation are encouraged to seek resolution through the following USDA procedures. Tier 1: Contracting Officer Concern Resolution Submission: Interested parties with concerns about either the solicitation or subsequent award should first submit their concern directly to the Contracting Officer, providing sufficient detail to allow the Contracting Officer to understand and assess the issue. Process: The Contracting Officer will review the concern, seek clarification as needed, and engage with the interested party to attempt prompt resolution. Review Timeline: The Contracting Officer will make every effort to provide a response or resolution within 10 business days of receiving the concern. Effect on Award or Performance: Tier 1 engagement is not considered an official notification of filing an agency protest and does not pause solicitation deadlines, delay award decisions, or suspend contract performance. Next Steps: If the matter cannot be resolved at Tier 1, the interested party may file a written agency protest under Tier 2. USDA encourages all parties to seek resolution with the Contracting Officer before filing an agency protest. Tier 2: Agency Protest If concerns cannot be resolved at Tier 1, an interested party may file a written agency protest with either the Contracting Officer or the USDA Independent Review Authority. The decision by the USDA Independent Review Authority is an alternative to a decision by the Contracting Officer. The USDA Independent Review Authority will not consider an appeal of the Contracting Officer�s decision on an agency protest. The protest must state whether the protester elects review by the Contracting Officer, by the UDSA Independent Review Authority. If no election is stated, the Contracting Officer will decide the protest. Required Information: Protests shall include the information set forth in FAR 33.104-4 (a)(3). Failure to submit the required information may result in a delay or dismissal of the protest. Submission: Agency protests should be submitted electronically to SPE.inquiry@usda.gov and the Contracting Officer. Timeliness: Protests must be filed within the timeframes specified in FAR 33.104. Effect on Award or Performance: Contract awards or performance will be suspended during the protest period unless justified in writing for urgent and compelling reasons or determined to be in the best interest of the Government. Review Timeline: USDA strives to resolve agency-level protests within 35 business days of receipt. Election of Forum: By filing a protest with USDA, the protesters agree not to file a protest on the same matter with the Government Accountability Office (GAO) or any other external forum while the agency protest is pending. If such a protest is filed externally, the USDA agency protest will be dismissed. Questions: Questions regarding this notice or protest procedures should be directed to the Contracting Officer identified in this solicitation.

description: THIS NOTICE IS FOR MARKET RESEARCH PURPOSES ONLY. This is not a solicitation, request for quotation, or commitment by the Government to issue a solicitation or award a contract. The Government will not pay for information submitted or reimburse respondents for costs incurred in responding to this notice. The Government is seeking information from capable sources regarding a commercially available, cloud-hosted software service to support food and beverage inventory management, purchasing, recipe and menu cost calculation, billing support, reporting, mobile barcode scanning, user training, system transition, and technical support for Government flight operations at Joint Base Andrews and authorized remote users. The anticipated requirement is further described in the attached draft Performance Work Statement. The Government is conducting market research to identify capable small and other-than-small business concerns, assess commercial practices and available contract vehicles, refine the requirement, and develop the acquisition strategy. No final set-aside determination has been made. Interested respondents should identify their business size and applicable socioeconomic status under the anticipated North American Industry Classification System code 513210, Software Publishers, subject to final Government determination. Interested firms shall submit a concise capability statement, not to exceed five pages, addressing their ability to meet the attached draft Performance Work Statement. Responses should include: Company name, address, point of contact, email address, telephone number, Unique Entity Identifier, and Commercial and Government Entity code, if available; Business size and socioeconomic status; Relevant experience providing comparable cloud-based inventory, purchasing, costing, billing, mobile scanning, training, transition, and support services; Up to three relevant prior or current contracts, including customer name, contract number, brief scope, period of performance, and point of contact, if release is authorized; Licensing approach, including named-user, concurrent-user, mobile-user, site, or enterprise licensing limitations; Capability to provide transition, configuration, account setup, data import or migration support, training, and technical support; Any assumptions, commercial limitations, third-party dependencies, or draft-PWS requirements that may materially affect capability, schedule, or pricing; Available Government contract vehicles through which the respondent�s solution may be ordered, including vehicle name, contract number, applicable category or special item number, and ordering eligibility; and For proposed teaming or subcontracting arrangements, the anticipated division of work between the prime contractor and team members, including the estimated percentage of effort to be subcontracted and the business size of proposed subcontractors. The Government will use the information received to identify capable sources, assess small-business capability, evaluate available contract vehicles, refine the draft requirement, and determine the appropriate acquisition strategy. Telephone responses will not be accepted. Submit responses electronically to raffaele.simpson.ctr@us.af.mil and antoine.toran.1@us.af.mil no later than time response date/time indicated via SAM sources sought posting. Interested parties shall review Attachment(s): Draft Performance Work Statement, and Sources-Sought Industry Response Template and PWS Feedback Questionnaire. The questionnaire requests capability information, commercial licensing and support practices, transition assumptions, available contract vehicles, nonbinding budgetary pricing, and recommended PWS revisions or clarification. Respondents should identify the applicable draft-PWS paragraph for any comment, ambiguity, commercial limitation, or suggested alternative approach. The Government may use responses to refine the requirement, validate the Independent Government Estimate, assess available sources and contract vehicles, and determine the acquisition strategy. title: Q515 - Notice of Intent to Sole-Source Requirement: Artera AI Prostate Exam Testing - Cleveland VAMC
description: Notice of Intent to Sole-Source Requirement The Department of Veterans Affairs, Network Contracting Office (NCO) 10, intends to negotiate a sole source contract under Simplified Acquisition Procedures and the authority of FAR 6.302-1, Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements. The associated NAICS code for this is 541380, Size Standard is $19 Million. Product Service Code (PSC) is Q515. The sole-source contract will be awarded to: ARTERA, INC UEI: S8PHW2AWT2R7 Description of requirements: The VA Northeast Ohio Healthcare System (VANEOHS) requires access to specialized multi-modal artificial intelligence (MMAI) prostate risk stratification testing of prostate biopsies or surgical specimens to assess the likelihood and severity of prostate recurrence or progression. Multi-modal artificial intelligence (MMAI) is a precision medicine platform designed to optimize cancer treatment, primarily for prostate and breast cancer patients. This testing consists of the following to generate patient specific prostate cancer risk stratification: Data Integration: Artera AI analyzes H&E-stained pathology slides alongside patient clinical information, such as age, tumor stage, and lab results; Predictive Modeling: The AI algorithm predicts which patients are likely to benefit from specific therapies, such as short-term androgen deprivation therapy (ST-ADT) in prostate cancer; Outcome Estimation: It estimates long-term outcomes, including disease progression and metastasis risk, helping clinicians tailor treatment plans Artera AI Prostate is the first MMAI test recommended in the NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines for prostate cancer. It identifies patients who may benefit most from hormone therapy and supports early-stage treatment decisions. Benefits of this testing are early intervention providing actionable insights to guide therapy selection and improve patient outcomes for our prostate cancer patients. It is the Government's belief that only the proposed candidate possesses the required capabilities to successfully meet this requirement. It is the Government's intention to solicit and negotiate with only this source. This notice of intent is not a request for competitive proposals. IAW FAR 5.207 all responsible sources may submit a capability statement, proposal, or quotation, which shall be considered by the agency. This is not a solicitation or request for offers. No solicitation package is available. Any response to this notice must show clear and convincing evidence that demonstrates the ability to comply with the requirement and that competition would be advantageous to the Government. The Government will not pay for information submitted. A determination not to compete based on responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. All responses to this intent to sole source must be emailed to Thomas Bellamy: thomas.bellamy@va.gov and Samantha Jarrett: samantha.jarrett@va.gov by 3:00 p.m. EST November 10th, 2026.

description: Sources Sought Notice Sources Sought Notice Page 5 of 5 Sources Sought Notice *= Required Field Sources Sought Notice Page 1 of 5 The VA Saint Louis Health Care System, John Cochran Division, requires a Construction Contractor to Construction Contractor to prepare existing space for a new PET/CT., at the John Cochran VAMC, 915 N Grand Blvd, St. Louis, MO 63106. This project has a set of drawings and specifications. These drawings and specifications indicate the work to be performed at the John Cochran VAMC and will be issued at time of solicitation. Solicitation will be issued on before December 2, 2026. Title: 657-24-102JC - Prepare Site for New PET/CT, Room A011D Solicitation Number: 36C25527R0016 Contracting Office: Network Contracting Office 15 Contracting Office Location: 3450 S 4th Street Traffic way, Leavenworth, Kansas Posted Date: 11/03/2026 Response Date: 11/10/2026 at 2:00 PM Central Time Set Aside: Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business Classification Code: Z2DA - Repair or Alteration of Hospitals and Infirmaries NAICS Code: 236220 Commercial and Institutional Building Construction Synopsis: Please note that this is NOT a request for quotes or proposals, the Government is seeking information for market research purposes only. The Government may or may not issue solicitation documents. The Department of Veterans Affairs Network Contracting Office (NCO) 15, is conducting a market survey for qualified: Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Businesses (SDVOSB), capable of providing the required services outlined below for the John Cochran VA Medical Center, Saint Louis, Missouri. The applicable NAICS code is 236220 Commercial and Institutional Building Construction and the size standard is $45.0 Million. Responses to this notice must be submitted via e-mail and received no later than November 10, 2026, at 2:00 PM Central Time. No telephone inquiries will be accepted or returned. Additional information about this project will be issued on the Federal Contract Opportunities website https://www.sam.gov once available. Period of Performance for base bid is 365 calendar days. In accordance with VARR 836.204, the estimated cost magnitude is between $1,000,000.00 and $2,000,000.00 Prospective SDVOSB firms are reminded that in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 52.219-14(e)(3), the Contractor agrees it will not pay more than 85 percent of the amount paid by the Government for contract performance, excluding the cost of materials, to subcontractors that are not similarly situated entities. Any work that a similarly situated entity further subcontracts will count towards the prime contractor's 85 percent subcontract amount that cannot be exceeded. GENERAL SCOPE OF WORK: Work includes, but is not limited to, general construction, alterations, mechanical, electrical & plumbing work, utility systems, fire protection systems, abatement work, necessary demolition and removal of existing structures, associated appurtenances, and certain other items necessary completion. All work shall be performed in accordance with solicitation/contract terms and conditions, specifications and drawings, and all applicable VA TIL and local and National codes. Contractor shall furnish all supervision, tools, labor, materials, equipment, transportation and testing necessary. Contractor will perform site investigations to fully inform themselves of the conditions and limitations applied to the work. The drawings and specifications include guidance on: Working hours allowed on this project. ICRA (Infection Control Risk Assessments) requirements and containment barriers. ILSM (Interim Life Safety Measures). Division of responsibilities between contractor and equipment vendor. This Statement of Work (SOW) is intended as an outline and is not a detailed summary of the work the contractor will be required to perform. In the event of conflict between this SOW and the project drawings and specifications, the drawings and specifications will take precedence over this SOW. END OF SCOPE OF WORK Interested firms must be registered in https://sam.gov with NAICS code 236220 and qualified as a Service Disabled Veteran Owned small business under 236220 Commercial and Institutional Building Construction. Qualified service-disabled veteran owned small businesses are encouraged to respond and required to be registered in with the Small Business Administration (SBA) registry https://veterans.certify.sba.gov on or before the response date. If interested in this opportunity, please provide Capability Statement via email. The Capability Statement is designed to inform the Department of Veteran Affairs of any prospective construction contractors' project execution capabilities. The submission is limited to 10 pages which shall include the following information: 1) Offeror's name, address, point of contact, phone number, e-mail address, and Unique Entity ID. 2) Offeror's interest in bidding on the solicitation when it is issued. 3) Offeror's capability to perform a contract of this magnitude and complexity and comparable work performed within the past 5 years - brief description of the project, customer name, timeliness of performance, customer satisfaction, and dollar value of the project - provide at least 1, but no more than 3 completed construction examples. 4) Offeror's CVE certification as a Veteran owned business. 5) Please provide Socio-economic status for NAICS code 236220 Commercial and Institutional Building Construction and provide percentage of self-performed labor your company can perform for this type of project. 6) Offeror's Joint Venture information if applicable - existing and potential. 7) Offeror's Bonding Capability in the form of a letter from Surety providing bonding level per contract and aggregate. No basis for claim against the Government shall arise as a result of a response to this sources sought or Government use of any information provided. The Government will not pay for information or comments provided and will not recognize any costs associated with submission of comments. There is no guarantee, expressed or implicit, that market research for this acquisition will result in a particular set-aside, or any other guarantee of award or acquisition strategy. Responses must be received by 2:00 PM Central on November 10, 2026, via e-mail to the Contracting Officer at Matthew.Finley@va.gov and Contract Specialist Abby.Monroe2@va.gov PLEASE REFERENCE "SOURCES SOUGHT: : 657-24-102JC - Prepare Site for New PET/CT, Room A011D , IN THE SUBJECT LINE and cover sheet. Respondents will not be contacted regarding their submission or information gathered as a result of this Sources Sought notice. Interested firms shall be required to respond to additional announcements separately from this announcement without further notice from the Government when posted to the Contract Opportunities website at https://sam.gov. The Contract Opportunities website is the only official site to obtain these documents. Contracting Office Address: Department of Veterans Affairs; Network 15 Contracting Office; 3450 S. 4th Street, Leavenworth, KS 66048 Point of Contact(s): Abby Monroe, Contract Specialist, e-mail address: Abby.Monroe2@va.gov

title: Nákup výpočetní techniky – monitory
description: Nákup a dodávka výpočetní techniky – 150 ks monitorů. Popis a minimální technické požadavky na funkcionalitu a vlastnosti požadovaných monitorů (dále jen „zboží“) jsou uvedeny v příloze č. 1 – technická specifikace předmětu koupě (dle technických standardů pro ICT komodity 2026 Ministerstva zdravotnictví ČR), která bude nedílnou současní realizační smlouvy. Zboží musí být nové a nabídková cena musí být konečná včetně dopravy a všech dalších nákladů dodavatele do Psychiatrické nemocnice v Opavě. Součástí nabídky dodavatele musí být katalogový list nabízeného zboží, z nějž bude možno odvodit technické parametry. Závazné obchodní, platební, záruční a další podmínky jsou uvedeny ve vzoru Smlouvy – návrhu obchodních a smluvních podmínek, který je přílohou těchto PPZN. Zařízení musí splňovat: Nařízení Komise EU č. 617/2013 ze dne 26. června 2013, kterým se provádí směrnice Evropského parlamentu a Rady 2009/2009/125/ES, soulad s direktivou RoHS (Restriction of Use of Certain Hazardous Substances), certifikát EPEAT (Electronic Product Environmental Assessment Tool), Energy Star min. 6.1. Podrobnosti jsou uvedeny v zadávací dokumentaci a jejich přílohách.

title: NCTAMS PAC CAIRS Support
description: The Defense Information Systems Agency/Defense Information Technology Contracting Organization intends to negotiate a sole source contract with Unique Communications Solutions. A sole source Justification & Approval document is being coordinated and, upon approval, a copy of it will be posted here on SAM.gov to comply with the public display requirements of FAR 6.301. The proposed contract action is for software access and continuous contracted maintenance support to keep Naval Computer and Telecommunications Area Master Station Pacific (NCTAMS PAC) subordinate sites Configuration Accounting Information Retrieval System (CAIRS) software packages current to meet JITC and IA security requirements in support of NCTAMS PAC regional BCO mission requirements. The current contract is in its fifth and final year. DITCO-PAC is establishing a new contract for one base year with four option periods. The consolidated contract supports Naval Computer and Telecommunications Station Far East (NCTS FE) to include Diego Garcia, NCTS Guam (NCTS GU), and NCTS San Diego (NCTS SD) and NCTS Detachment Puget Sound (NCTS PS). In Option Year One, services will include NCTAMS PAC in Wahiawa, Hawaii. The NCTAMS PAC Hawaii infrastructure is currently being installed and accredited at the estimated time of award and is not projected to need services/support until Q3/Q4 of 2027. At this time, the incumbent contractor Unique Communications Solutions is the only source capable of providing all necessary services for the NCTAMS PAC area of responsibility (AOR). Unique Communications Solutions is the sole OEM provider for the Configuration Accounting Information Retrieval System (CAIRS). The CAIRS system is unique in its functionality and features. There are no other companies that provide a system that has the exact components and abilities. CAIRS is trademarked through Unique Communications Solutions only. The Software Upgrade Kits are specific to the software they support. Unique Communications Solutions is the only company that can directly perform the following with the CAIRS programs: Upgrades, Update, Add Features, Fix Software problems, provide standard maintenance, Give training and technical support, Onsite Installation and Training. The statutory authority for other than full and open competition is 10 USC 2304 (c) (1), as implemented by FAR 6.302-1(c)(2), only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements. Companies who believe they can provide this service must indicate their interest in writing within 5 days of this notification and include a detailed capability statement. No reimbursement for any cost connected with providing capability information will be provided. All responsible sources will be considered in evaluating the determination to issue a sole-source contract. Quotations or proposals received in response to this notice cannot be accepted since this synopsis cannot be considered a request for quote or a request for proposal. A solicitation will NOT be posted to SAM.gov due to the sole source nature of the requirement. The North American Classification System (NAICS) code 541519 will be used for determining company size status. title: UT NP ARCH 100(2) Bridges on Delicate Arch Road
description: PROJECT NUMBER: UT NP ARCH 100(2) PROJECT NAME: Bridges on Delicate Arch Road PROJECT DESCRIPTION: Delicate Arch Road (DAR) is within Arches National Park (Park) and provides access to Delicate Arch. DAR is a functional class 1 roadway (Principal Park Road) and is heavily traveled by visitors and often congested during periods with moderate-to-high levels of visitation. DAR crosses three low-gradient ephemeral washes (Salt Valley Wash, Salt Wash, and Winter Camp Wash) near their confluence in the Salt Wash Basin downstream of Wolfe Ranch. Culverts installed during original road construction in the mid-1990s and during subsequent upgrades are inadequate to allow unobstructed stream flow and sediment transport downstream. This existing condition produces flooding and sediment deposition, which creates unsafe conditions for visitors, triggers road closures, potentially strands Park visitors, diminishes visitor experience of the Park, and generates high operational costs associated with traffic management, visitor safety, and cleanup operations. SCOPE OF THE WORK: This project will be designated as Reconstruction (4R) with one segment of restoration (3R), and will design and construct 100� span concrete bridges at the Salt Valley Wash, Salt Wash, and Winter Camp Wash. The DA roadway profile at each Wash will be raised to accommodate a 10-year design frequency and allow a medium-sized excavator to access each wash. The DA will be realigned at the Salt Valley wash, moving the roadway and new bridge location to the north of the existing roadway and drainage crossing. The remaining 3R sections of the roadway will receive full depth reclamation (FDR) or removal of pavement, including all parking areas, followed by a 4-inch pavement overlay. PRINCIPAL WORK ITEMS: 20420-0000 Embankment Construction: 10,000 CUYD 25101-0300 Placed Riprap, Class 3: 1,725 CUYD 30202-2000 Roadway Aggregate, Method 2: 5,140 TON 40101-5600 Asphalt Concrete Pavement, Gyratory Mix, 1/2-Inch or 3/4-Inch Nominal Maximum Size Aggregate, 0.3 To <3 Million ESAL: 8,300 TON 55201-0200 Structural Concrete, Class A (AE): 752 CUYD 55401-2000 Reinforcing Steel, Epoxy Coated: 138,000 LB 55601-1100 Bridge Railing, Steel, Two Rail: 642 LNFT 56501-0200 Drilled Shaft, 24-Inch Diameter: 750 LNFT 56501-0300 Drilled Shaft, 30-Inch Diameter: 890 LNFT 60901-1300 Curb, Concrete, 15-Inch Depth (Reinforced, Colored): 3,921 LNFT 61701-4500 Guardrail System Mgs, Type 2, Class A Steel Posts: 1,290 LNFT 63506-0500 Temporary Traffic Control, Flagger: 5,800 HOUR ANTICIPATED SCHEDULE: Advertisement � September 2026 Award � November 2026 NTP � December 2026 Contract Completion � December 2028 ESTIMATED COST RANGE: Total estimated cost between $10,000,000 and $20,000,000 This will be solicited as a full and open competition.

title: AN/UPX-50 Common Core Digital Interrogator (CCDI) Productionization
description: The Naval Air Systems Command (NAVAIR) intends to award a sole source, Cost Plus Fixed Fee (CPFF) Basic Ordering Agreement (BOA) order under N0001922G0009 to BAE Systems Information and Electronic Systems Integration, Inc. of Greenlawn, NY. This order is for the productionization of the AN/UPX-52 Common Core Digital Interrogator (CCDI). This includes transitioning from lab-built prototypes to units that can be produced in an electronics manufacturing environment, the development of unique CCDI test equipment and procedures, as well as integration of the CCDI into existing DI test equipment to ensure the CCDI meets all specified requirements. Lastly, this effort includes Automated Switch-Over (ASO) production line development, a CCDI Re-Spin option, and a CCDI Unknown Trouble Report (TR) corrections option. The anticipated total value of this order is $47M with an award estimated in Q4 of 2026. The period of performance is expected to be 32 months from date of award. The place of performance is anticipated to be at BAE Systems� facility in Greenlawn, New York. This pre-solicitation notice is published for informational purposes only. THIS NOTICE IS NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE PROPOSALS. This requirement will be procured in accordance with the statutory authority at 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1), as implemented by FAR 6.302?1, only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements. BAE Systems is the sole designer, developer, and manufacturer of the AN/UPX-45 and AN/UPX-50 DI systems. As such, they are the only company that has the requisite knowledge and technical data necessary to meet this requirement. The Government does not possess a complete technical data package for these systems. The required technical data to complete the software updates are proprietary to BAE systems. The Government does not intend to use the provisions of FAR Part 12 for this acquisition. Firms interested in subcontracting opportunities may contact Andrea Michialis at BAE at andrea.michialis@baesystems.com. Pipefitter shall have minimum one year of experience at the Journeyman level laying out, fabricating, assembling, installing, maintaining piping systems in a commercial, industrial, or hospital setting. Pipefitter shall have experience in assembling selecting and preparing appropriate materials for the application and assembling utilizing threading, soldering, brazing methods. Additional required experience monitoring chemical levels in water and proportioning chemicals to maintain required levels. Ability to perform minor steam fitting, plumbing, electrical work, painting, and housekeeping of the utility plant. The Contractor shall notify the Contracting Officer (CO), in writing, within 15 calendar days after the occurrence of any of these events and provide the information required below. After 90 days, the Contractor shall submit the information required below to the CO at least 15 calendar days prior to making any permanent substitutions. The Contractor shall provide a detailed explanation of the circumstances necessitating the proposed substitutions, complete resumes for the proposed substitutes, and any additional information requested by the CO. Proposed substitutes shall have comparable qualifications to those of the persons being replaced. The CO will notify the Contractor within 15 calendar days after receipt of all required information of the decision on the proposed substitutes. The contract will be modified to reflect any approved changes of key personnel. For temporary substitutions where the key person will not report to work for three (3) consecutive work days or more, the Contractor shall provide a qualified replacement for the key person. The substitute shall have comparable qualifications to the key person. Any period exceeding two weeks will require the procedure as stated above. title: Aircraft Coatings and Sealants OO-ALC
description: The Ogden Air Logistics Complex (OO-ALC) at Hill Air Force Base, Utah, has a need to contract for comprehensive management and supply of aircraft coatings and sealants. This effort aims to ensure uninterrupted aircraft maintenance operations through robust inventory management, timely delivery, and technical support. This effort will include frequent ordering and quick delivery of specified items. The selected contractor will be responsible for continuous deliveries and support of Coatings and Sealants, including: 1. Order Fulfillment and Material Handling: Sourcing, storing, and delivering all required coatings and sealants (see attached list). This includes meeting a strict four (4) hour delivery timeline for urgent requirements and handling specialized materials, such as Premixed Frozen Material (PFM) requiring transit at -80F. The contractor must maintain a minimum of 85% shelf life for all products upon delivery. The contractor will also be responsible for managing shelf-life and ensuring proper storage and handling of the products prior to delivery.2. FMS-3600 Coating Management: For this specialized product, implementing a lock and key ITAR-compliant storage system and maintaining rigorous chain of custody for the material.3. Technical Assistance: Providing technical assistance that includes rapid response (within one business day) to material failures, on-site technical support during monthly visits, product change support, and quality audit reporting.4. Online Ordering System: Furnishing a secure, web-based ordering and tracking system with real-time visibility of lead times and minimum stock levels (MSLS).5. Ramp-Up Plan: Executing a ramp-up plan to achieve full performance readiness within eight (8) months of contract award. The anticipated contract will be a Firm Fixed Priced (FFP) IDIQ to include an 8-month ramp up period, a 5-year ordering period, and a 6-month allowance for remaining deliveries on the back end. Total period of performance is anticipated to be 6 years and 2 months. This is a total small business set-aside. The Government anticipates awarding a single contract. All interested small businesses are encouraged to respond to this solicitation. The Government intends to award a single contract resulting from the solicitation to the responsible offeror whose proposal represents the best value to the Government. This effort requires Contractors to be CMMC level 2 self-certified, therefore if you are not currently level 2 certified and are interested in this requirement you will need to begin the process to become level 2 certified immediately. Contract period of performance dates on the solicitation are estimates and are subject to change according to when the effort gets awarded. title: UT NP ARCH 100(2) Bridges on Delicate Arch Road
description: PROJECT NUMBER: UT NP ARCH 100(2) PROJECT NAME: Bridges on Delicate Arch Road PROJECT DESCRIPTION: Delicate Arch Road (DAR) is within Arches National Park (Park) and provides access to Delicate Arch. DAR is a functional class 1 roadway (Principal Park Road) and is heavily traveled by visitors and often congested during periods with moderate-to-high levels of visitation. DAR crosses three low-gradient ephemeral washes (Salt Valley Wash, Salt Wash, and Winter Camp Wash) near their confluence in the Salt Wash Basin downstream of Wolfe Ranch. Culverts installed during original road construction in the mid-1990s and during subsequent upgrades are inadequate to allow unobstructed stream flow and sediment transport downstream. This existing condition produces flooding and sediment deposition, which creates unsafe conditions for visitors, triggers road closures, potentially strands Park visitors, diminishes visitor experience of the Park, and generates high operational costs associated with traffic management, visitor safety, and cleanup operations. SCOPE OF THE WORK: This project will be designated as Reconstruction (4R) with one segment of restoration (3R), and will design and construct 100� span concrete bridges at the Salt Valley Wash, Salt Wash, and Winter Camp Wash. The DA roadway profile at each Wash will be raised to accommodate a 10-year design frequency and allow a medium-sized excavator to access each wash. The DA will be realigned at the Salt Valley wash, moving the roadway and new bridge location to the north of the existing roadway and drainage crossing. The remaining 3R sections of the roadway will receive full depth reclamation (FDR) or removal of pavement, including all parking areas, followed by a 4-inch pavement overlay. PRINCIPAL WORK ITEMS: 20420-0000 Embankment Construction: 10,000 CUYD 25101-0300 Placed Riprap, Class 3: 1,725 CUYD 30202-2000 Roadway Aggregate, Method 2: 5,140 TON 40101-5600 Asphalt Concrete Pavement, Gyratory Mix, 1/2-Inch or 3/4-Inch Nominal Maximum Size Aggregate, 0.3 To <3 Million ESAL: 8,300 TON 55201-0200 Structural Concrete, Class A (AE): 752 CUYD 55401-2000 Reinforcing Steel, Epoxy Coated: 138,000 LB 55601-1100 Bridge Railing, Steel, Two Rail: 642 LNFT 56501-0200 Drilled Shaft, 24-Inch Diameter: 750 LNFT 56501-0300 Drilled Shaft, 30-Inch Diameter: 890 LNFT 60901-1300 Curb, Concrete, 15-Inch Depth (Reinforced, Colored): 3,921 LNFT 61701-4500 Guardrail System Mgs, Type 2, Class A Steel Posts: 1,290 LNFT 63506-0500 Temporary Traffic Control, Flagger: 5,800 HOUR ANTICIPATED SCHEDULE: Advertisement � September 2026 Award � November 2026 NTP � December 2026 Contract Completion � December 2028 ESTIMATED COST RANGE: Total estimated cost between $10,000,000 and $20,000,000 This will be solicited as a full and open competition.

title: P-8A Australian APY-10 Radar Regional Repair Facility
description: The Naval Air Systems Command (NAVAIR) intends to issue a sole source delivery order to The Raytheon Company, Space and Airborne Systems Division, McKinney, TX, to establish a regional P-8A APY-10 radar repair and diagnostic capability in Australia in support of United States Navy, Royal Australian Air Force, and approved regional partner P-8A operations. The effort is expected to include: Relocation of existing Antenna Control Electronics (ACE) and Antenna (ANT) Diagnostic Test Equipment from Fleet Readiness Center Southeast (FRC-SE) to a new facility in Australia; the establishment of repair capabilities for two of the five Weapon Replaceable Assemblies (WRAs); Field Service Representative (FSR) support for the transition, logistics, and initial operator training; the procurement, build, and delivery of a new System Integration Level Test Set (SILTS) to provide a complete five-out-of-five WRA test and repair capability; and the procurement of a new Flight Line Systems Diagnostics (FLSD) system. The anticipated period of performance is Q2 FY2027 through Q2 FY2032 with award anticipated in Q2 FY2027. These requirements will be procured in accordance with the statutory authority permitting other than full and open competition under Title 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1) as implemented by FAR 6.103-1, "Only One Responsible Source and No other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements." Raytheon is the sole designer, developer, and manufacturer of these Systems with the requisite knowledge, experience, and technical data that can meet the Government requirements on a timely basis. THIS NOTICE IS NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE PROPOSALS. Interested parties may, however, identify their interest and capability by responding to the requirement. The Government will consider all information received prior to the closing of this synopsis. Information received will be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. A determination by the Government not to compete the proposed contract action is solely at the discretion of the Government. No phone inquiries will be entertained. Responses shall be made in writing by E-mail or U.S. Mail to the attention of Jessica Dean, contract specialist or Ron Hickman, Procuring Contracting Officer using the contact information provided with this synopsis. However, the Government will consider all responses received within fifteen days after the publication date of this synopsis. Companies interested in subcontracting opportunities should contact Raytheon directly via Scott McCrory via scott.mccrory@rtx.com.

title: AN/UPX-50 Common Core Digital Interrogator (CCDI) Productionization
description: This Synopsis is being reposted for administrative purposes only. The Naval Air Systems Command (NAVAIR) intends to award a sole source, Cost Plus Fixed Fee (CPFF) BOA order to BAE Systems Information and Electronic Systems Integration of Greenlawn, NY (BAE) for the productionization of the AN/UPX-50 Common Core Digital Interrogator (CCDI), Part Number (P/N) 8605800-1. The AN/UPX-50 CCDI is an update to the AN/UPX-50(C) DI to address obsolescence issues and to combine the AN/UPX-24 and the Digital Interrogator into one system due to can build restraints and crypto certification. BAE, as the sole designer, developer, and manufacturer of the AN/UPX-50(C) DI is the only company with the unique knowledge, experience, special skills, facilities, manufacturing techniques, and technical data required to perform these requirements. This acquisition is being pursued on a sole source basis under the statutory authority of 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1), as implemented by Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 6.302-1, "Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements." The Government does not intend to use the provisions of FAR Part 12 for this acquisition. Firms interested in subcontracting opportunities may contact Andrea Michialis at BAE at andrea.michialis@baesystems.com.

title: Germany – Engineering design services – Gemeinde Stralendorf - Neubau der Kindertagesstätte "Regenbogen"
description: Die Gemeinde Stralendorf (Eigentümer/Bauherr) plant den Neubau der Kindertagesstätte Regenbogen als Ersatz für die bestehende Einrichtung als eigenständiges Gebäude auf dem direkt angrenzenden Grundstück für 40 Kinder (28 Kindergarten- und 12 Krippenkinder). Durch den geplanten Neubau sollen sich die Betreuungs- und Rahmenbedingungen für die Kinder und Erzieherinnen verbessern. Im neuen Gebäude ist geplant, 1 Krippenbereich für 12 Kinder sowie 2 Kitabereiche für je 14 Kinder anzubieten, so dass insgesamt 40 Kinder die Einrichtung in Stralendorf besuchen können. Die Möglichkeit einer Erweiterung um 8 Kinder (1 Mischgruppe) soll hierbei Berücksichtigung finden. Die geplante Nettogrundfläche von 328 qm entspricht der maximal zulässigen Fläche für die Entgeldberechnung. Als Gebäudestandort wird das vorhandene Grundstück (Flurstück 135/21, Flur 2) mit einer Größe von ca. 1.600 qm genutzt, ohne die bestehenden Freiflächen und -anlagen der jetzigen Kindertagesstätte zu beeinträchtigen. Diese bleiben erhalten und sollen weiterhin als Außenspielflächen genutzt werden. Das Ortsbild der Gemeinde ist in diesem Bereich durch eingeschossige Gebäude mit Sattel- und Krüppelwalmdächern sowie Nebengebäude und Anbauten mit unterschiedlichen Dachformen geprägt. Der geplante eingeschossige Baukörper der neuen Kindertagesstätte mit den flach geneigten Satteldächern soll sich harmonisch in das Dorfbild einfügen. Gegenstand dieser Ausschreibung sind Ingenieurleistungen gemäß HOAI 2021 Teil 4 Fachplanung, Abschnitt 2 Technische Ausrüstung, Anlagengruppen 1-3,Leistungsphasen 1 - 4, Leistungsphase 5-9 optional (Stufenvertrag) Die Beauftragung der Stufe 1 (LPH 1-4) erfolgt sofort, die Beauftragung der Stufe 2 (LPH 5-9) erfolgt nach Bewilligung von Fördermitteln. title: Rakennus- ja purkutyöt sis. asbesti
description: Rakennus- ja purkutyöt sis. asbesti Kotkan-Haminan seudun koulutuskuntayhtymä, eli Ekami (hankintayksikkö, tilaaja) pyytää tarjouksia yksikköhintaisista rakennus- ja purkutöistä tarjouspyynnön ja sen liitteiden mukaisesti. Kiinteistöihin kohdistuvat työt ovat tuntitöinä laskutettavia, olemassa olevien kiinteistöjen korjaus-, kunnossapito- ja muutostöitä. Työnjohdosta vastaa toimittaja. Rakennus- ja purkutöihin kuuluvat työt jokaisella Ekamin kampuksella. Kampukset sijaitsevat: - Koteko: Kymenlaaksonkatu 29, 48100 Kotka - Katariina: Lehmustie 4, 48130 Kotka - Malminki: Malminginkatu 4-8, 48600 Kotka - Hamina: Kadettikoulunkatu 18, 49400 Hamina Hankintamenettelyllä muodostetaan kahden (2) + yhden (1) optiovuoden mittainen puitejärjestely, johon valitaan neljä (4) toimittajaa. Puitejärjestelyyn valitaan toimittajat tarjousvertailun perusteella syntyneessä kokonaistaloudellisessa edullisuusjärjestyksessä. Hankintayksikkö pidättää oikeuden muodostaa puitejärjestely, vaikka soveltuvuusvaatimukset täyttäviä tarjouksia tulisi vähemmän kuin neljä. Tilaajalla on oikeus yksipuolisella päätöksellä jatkaa kahden (2) vuoden määräaikaista puitesopimuskautta ottamalla käyttöön yhden (1) vuoden mittaisen option. Tilaaja ilmoittaa optiokauden käyttöönotosta kirjallisesti viimeistään 3 kk ennen määräaikaisen sopimuskauden päättymistä. Mikäli tilaaja ottaa option käyttöön, pätevät nyt kilpailutettavan sopimuksen ehdot sellaisenaan myös siihen. Hankinta toteutetaan puitejärjestelynä, koska hankittavien palvelujen määrää ja täsmällistä sisältöä ei pystytä arvioimaan etukäteen. Hankintayksikkö ei sitoudu tiettyihin hankintamääriin sopimuskauden aikana. Palveluita tilataan sopimusaikana tarpeiden ja määrärahojen puitteissa. Toimeksiantokohtaiset tavoitteet määritetään kussakin kohteessa erikseen. Tilaaja voi hankkia sopimuksen puitteissa puitejärjestelykumppaneilta myös saneeraus- ja uudisrakennusurakoihin sisältyviä, hankinnan kohteena olevia sähkötöitä, mutta sopimus ei muodosta puitejärjestelykumppaneille yksinoikeutta rakennusurakoiden sisällä tehtäviin sähkötöihin. Osa-, rinnakkais- tai vaihtoehtoiset tarjoukset eivät ole sallittuja.,

title: Høyttalersystem
description: Kongsberg kommune ved Kongsberg Musikkteater har til formål å kjøpe inn nytt høyttalersystem til bruk i Musikkteater-salen. Kongsberg Musikkteater har behov for et driftssikkert og høykvalitets høyttalersystem. Systemet skal levere lyd av høyeste kvalitet i samsvar med dagens krav, og skal kunne reprodusere alle musikksjangere på en overbevisende måte. Det skal være nok «headroom» slik at systemet tåler all slags bruk, med jevn dekning i hele publikumsområdet. Det er svært viktig for Kongsberg Musikkteater at høyttalersystemet er allment akseptert, det vil si at systemet er i henhold til krav fra både norske og internasjonale artister og produksjoner. Høyttalersystemet inkluderer et L/R hovedhøyttalersystem på hver side av scenen, subwoofere, DSP og nødvendig tilbehør. Det vil også være behov for frontfill for å gi jevn dekning frem mot scenekant. For oppheng stiller oppdragsgiver med justerbare opphengspunkter. Salens publikumskapasitet er ca. 630 sittende personer med skyvbart amfi og ca. 1050 stående publikummere når amfiet trekkes inn. De første 3 radene kan fjernes når orkestergraven skal benyttes eller ved stående publikum. Kongsberg Musikkteater stiller med personlift til bruk under installasjon. Fullstendig beskrivelse av leveransen følger av kravspesifikasjonen.

title: Aircraft Coatings and Sealants OO-ALC
description: The Ogden Air Logistics Complex (OO-ALC) at Hill Air Force Base, Utah, has a need to contract for comprehensive management and supply of aircraft coatings and sealants. This effort aims to ensure uninterrupted aircraft maintenance operations through robust inventory management, timely delivery, and technical support. This effort will include frequent ordering and quick delivery on specified items. The selected contractor will be responsible for continuous deliveries and support of Coatings and Sealants, including: 1. Order Fulfillment and Material Handling: Sourcing, storing, and delivering all required coatings and sealants (see attached list). This includes meeting a strict four (4) hour delivery timeline for urgent requirements and handling specialized materials, such as Premixed Frozen Material (PFM) requiring transit at -80F. The contractor must maintain a minimum of 85% shelf life for all products upon delivery. The contractor will also be responsible for managing shelf-life and ensuring proper storage and handling of the products prior to delivery. 2. FMS-3600 Coating Management: For this specialized product, implementing a lock and key ITAR-compliant storage system and maintaining rigorous chain of custody for the material. 3. Technical Assistance: Providing technical assistance that includes rapid response (within one business day) to material failures, on-site technical support during monthly visits, product change support, and quality audit reporting. 4. Online Ordering System: Furnishing a secure, web-based ordering and tracking system with real-time visibility of lead times and minimum stock levels (MSLS). 5. Ramp-Up Plan: Executing a ramp-up plan to achieve full performance readiness within eight (8) months of contract award. The anticipated contract will be a Firm Fixed Priced (FFP) IDIQ to include an 8-month ramp up period, a 5-year ordering period, and a 6-month allowance for remaining deliveries on the back end. Total period of performance is anticipated to be 6 years and 2 months. This is a total small business set-aside. The Government anticipates awarding a single contract. All interested small businesses are encouraged to respond to this solicitation. The Government intends to award a single contract resulting from the solicitation to the responsible offeror whose proposal represents the best value to the Government. This effort requires Contractors to be CMMC level 2 self-certified, therefore if you are not currently level 2 certified and are interested in this requirement you will need to begin the process to become level 2 certified immediately. Contract period of performance dates on the solicitation are estimates and are subject to change according to when the effort gets awarded. title: Communications and Information Capabilities Secure Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) Data Platform Support Services
description: 1. DESCRIPTION U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) is conducting market research through a Request for Information (RFI) on the current availability and technological capabilities of vendors to provide identify commercial capabilities and potential sources that can provide secure Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) data platform support services to U.S. Border Patrol (USBP) personnel to successfully operate at Communications and Information Capabilities (CIC) Program. THE GOVERNMENT DOES NOT INTEND TO AWARD A CONTRACT ON THE BASIS OF THIS RFI OR TO OTHERWISE PAY FOR INFORMATION RECEIVED. This RFI is issued solely for information, planning purposes, and market research only; it does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP) or a promise to issue an RFP. This research does not commit the Government to contract for any supply or service. CBP will not pay any costs associated with responding to this research. Not responding to this RFI does not preclude participation in any future full and open competition RFP. If a solicitation is released, it will be posted to the SAM.gov (sam.gov) website. All submissions become the property of the Government and will not be returned. The information obtained from industry responses to this RFI may be used in the development of an acquisition strategy and future RFP. 2. INTRODUCTION CBP is responsible for securing the United States� national borders against the illegal entry of people and goods between Ports of Entry (POE). To accomplish this mission, the U.S. Border Patrol (USBP) employs infrastructure, technology, and personnel to predict and deter illicit activity, detect and track illegal border crossings, identify and classify incursions, and respond effectively. The CIC Program supports mission stakeholders through secure information-management, data-sharing, analytics, and technology-enabled collaboration capabilities. The Program is exploring options to obtain secure SaaS data platform support services that can meet evolving operational, data-management, cybersecurity, and user-support needs. The Government is interested in commercial solutions and associated managed services that maximize use of configurable, secure, and scalable SaaS capabilities while minimizing unnecessary custom development. The anticipated support services may include platform implementation, configuration, administration, data integration, data governance, security support, user support, training, reporting, and transition services. Where authorized by the Government, the platform may need to interoperate with existing Department of Homeland Security (DHS) identity, collaboration, cloud, data-management, and information-sharing services. To achieve comprehensive surveillance coverage, CBP requires autonomous systems, real-time intelligence integration, and persistent monitoring of high-priority zones. The CIC Program addresses these needs by delivering automated, location-determinant surveillance, integrating sensor data, and operationalizing censoring and optic infrastructure across critical areas. 3. PURPOSE The CIC Program seeks information from industry regarding the availability, maturity, implementation approach, security posture, operational support model, and pricing structures for secure SaaS data platform capabilities. The anticipated platform would support authorized users in securely ingesting, managing, governing, analyzing, sharing, and reporting on organizational data. 4. CURRENT STATUS / REQUIREMENTS CBP seeks information on industry capabilities to provide some or all the following services. 4.1 Technical Requirements a. Platform Implementation and Configuration Potential services include: Platform discovery, requirements refinement, and implementation planning. Platform configuration and tenant administration. Configuration of dashboards, reports, workflows, data models, and user roles. Environment setup, release planning, and deployment support. Development and maintenance of technical, operational, and user documentation. Support for platform modernization and enhancement efforts. b. Platform Operations and Administration Potential services include: Day-to-day SaaS platform administration. User account, role, group, and permissions management. Configuration management and documentation. Performance, availability, capacity, and utilization monitoring. Release, patch, and upgrade coordination. Change, incident, problem, and service-request management. Coordination with SaaS providers, Government stakeholders, and authorized third parties. c. Data Integration and Engineering Potential services include: Assessment and onboarding of approved data sources. Development, configuration, and sustainment of data pipelines, connectors, application programming interfaces, and data exchanges. Secure batch and near-real-time data ingestion, as applicable. Data transformation, validation, reconciliation, and quality monitoring. Data schema and metadata management. Error handling, logging, monitoring, and recovery support. Support for data export, migration, retention, archival, and disposition, as directed by the Government. d. Data Governance and Management Potential services include: Data cataloging and metadata management. Data lineage, provenance, and traceability support. Data-quality monitoring and remediation support. Data-access workflow support. Data stewardship and data-owner support. Support for Government-directed data labels, handling caveats, sharing restrictions, and retention requirements. Support for records-management processes, including legal holds, retention, archival, disposition, and deletion, as applicable. e. Cybersecurity, Privacy, and Compliance Support The Government is interested in solutions and services that support applicable DHS security, privacy, and cloud-computing requirements. Potential support areas include: Role-based access control and least-privilege access. Multi-factor authentication and single sign-on or identity federation. Encryption of data in transit and at rest using Government-approved methods. Audit logging, monitoring, alerting, and reporting. Security configuration management and secure baselines. Vulnerability-management coordination and remediation tracking. Security incident reporting and corrective-action support. Security assessment evidence collection and continuous-monitoring support. Privacy compliance support, as directed by the Government. Separation of Government data from other customer data in a multi-tenant environment. Support for applicable Federal security authorization processes. 4.2 Information Sharing and Interoperability The Government is interested in capabilities that support secure, controlled information sharing and interoperability with Government-approved systems and services. Potential capabilities include: Secure application programming interfaces, data feeds, file exchange, and web-service integrations. Identity federation and approved user-provisioning mechanisms. Controlled sharing of approved dashboards, reports, data products, documents, notifications, and collaboration artifacts. Segmentation of data and content by authorized organization, role, community, or other Government-defined criteria. Logging and auditability of data sharing, administrative activity, and user access. Interface documentation, test support, operational monitoring, and change management. 4.3 User Support and Training Potential services include: Tier 1, Tier 2, and Tier 3 user and administrator support. Incident intake, tracking, escalation, resolution, and closure. Service-request fulfillment. User onboarding, role modification, suspension, and deprovisioning support. Knowledge articles, user guides, frequently asked questions, and administrator documentation. End-user, administrator, and technical training.
